All right. Where's the Persian Empire? Egypt, Anatolia, the Levant, Mesopotamia—that’s Persia. So this is like the entire world and a small army, basically Macedonians only. This small army was able to conquer all of it. The question then is how? Well, similar to how the Qing conquered the Zhou and Chu because of elite competition and overproduction within these areas. These elites had no loyalty; they switched sides frequently.

So what probably happened was that certain elites invited Alexander to come over and he switched sides quickly, bulldozing through. Remember, when you reach an equilibrium, you become lazy, stupid, and arrogant. Darius is now the king of kings leading Persians but believed Alexander would stop at some point. "You have Egypt, the Levant, Anatolia, parts of Mesopotamia. I'll give you all this territory plus half my treasury." But Alexander was not like that. He considered himself a son of God and believed he had an unlimited appetite for conquest.

Darius died; Alexander kept going until he killed Darius and conquered the entire Persian Empire. However, Alexander was being co-opted by the Persian elite, inviting more into his army and administration, upsetting his Macedonian soldiers who assassinated him. The world then divided among his generals, creating what we call the Hellenistic age.

The world now combines Jewish, Greek, and Persian cultures in syncretism, which gives birth to Christianity. Once the Greeks control the world, they do so through religion and culture. Aristotle, Macedonian and childhood friend of Philip II, played a crucial role. Philip conquered Greece; Aristotle learned intellectual innovations from Plato at the academy. The Macedonians had a plan for a long time: Philip would learn military innovations in Greece while Aristotle would learn intellectual ones, systemizing Greek knowledge into an empire’s knowledge.
